name: Suiran, A Luxury Collection Hotel
positioning: Suiran, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Kyoto: a riverside hotel on the Hozu River in Arashiyama, built around an 1899 villa, with private hot spring baths
best_for: Travelers who want a quiet riverside base within walking distance of Arashiyama's main sights
Couples who want a room with its own onsen hot spring bath

facts.text: The hotel is set along the Hozu River in the Arashiyama Hills of Kyoto.
The hotel is within walking distance of Arashiyama's main sights.
Kyo-Suiran is housed in a villa built in 1899 by Baron Shozo Kawasaki as his summerhouse, combining Meiji Era architecture with contemporary lighting and seating.
The Kyo-Suiran residence has vaulted ceilings with exposed beams made of entire tree trunks, shoji screens, original art and calligraphy by Masayoshi Matsukata.
Pebble-stone pathways lead to the modern low-rise buildings that house the rooms.
Rooms are entered through a sliding door, and shoes are left at the entrance.
The spa treatment rooms sit in a secluded Japanese garden and feature a traditional open-air bath fed by hot spring water.
The spa offers green tea scrubs, jade stone facial treatments and collagen masks, in a private spa or in your room.
Guests can book a private session in the hotel's two cedar baths, Raku and An.
Kyo-Suiran serves washoku cuisine prepared in the French style, using local ingredients.
The hotel offers a complimentary Art Tour of the historic sites and art works on its premises.
Staff in yukata welcome guests with a hot towel and tea.

highlights.text: Some rooms have their own in-room onsen hot spring bath, and a Private Spa Room with an open-air bath is also available.
The Suiran Presidential Suite has bespoke furnishings and a private open-air bath with views.
Cafe Hassui is in a 100-year-old building erected for 19th-century poets, with calligraphic poems on its walls; every Friday morning the concierge leads a poem-tracing session there.
Every evening, complimentary free-flowing champagne and wine are offered at Cafe Hassui, with views of Arashiyama and the Hozu River.

considerations.text: There is no dedicated bar at the hotel.
The rooms do not have a work space.
WhataHotel notes the location means travel time to central Kyoto attractions.
